feat(onchain): witness-minimal fault statements + tier-2 re-hash exit measurement (#572)

Spec §12 fault statements: constant-width wire form (55-byte item statement),
fail-closed re-encode decoder, domain-separated commitment, tx_id-bound
adjudication. Per-asset conservation via two opaque single-invocation sweeps
(OutputUnitSweepV1 / MintUnitSweepV1) — item-0 opener rule, is_final
fail-closed on budget exhaustion, cross-round key-order enforcement. §12.5
ledgers the tier-2 re-hash measurement at the 13.2M basis (fixed-stride delta
91,697 = 0.70%; variable-width 29,298,758 = 2.22x basis — not resumable under
tier-2 carriage). §12.6 guard table: 39 guards, all neutralisation-confirmed.
Machine lane green under the fork runner: 367/367 across the native_tx suites
(fault-statement 48, machine-walk 46, intra-item 52, field-access 105+22+62).
validation-machine mint fixtures re-enveloped per #567 (27 -> 21 pre-existing
failures, zero regressions; stage-six flat-vs-counted tripwire pinned for
#575-#578).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): intra-item package — Value bookmark, Canonical-Data Acceptor, native-script pushdown (#571)

The Phase-3b intra-item access package, worked as one unit in the machine
lane, plus §11 written into docs/spec/midgard-tx.md — the section #566
reserved and #570 deliberately did not encroach on.

Case A — Value bookmark (native-tx-intra-item-v1.ak). Ordered intra-item
access into a multiasset value without materialising the output. 64 lookups
over 8 policies x 8 assets cost 12.22M mem against the 13,200,000-mem
GOAL_SPEC §3.3 basis; the materialising control costs 20.15M and does not
fit. The two are pinned to the same 64 answers, so the comparison means
something. The gap decomposes as 6.10M fixed plus 1.83M marginal — recorded
that way rather than as a single headline, because the fixed decode dominates
and `decode_canonical_output` also decides datum and script_ref, which the
bookmark never inspects.

Case B — Canonical-Data Acceptor. Datum interior access at 0.93M and 4.87M,
both far inside the basis. Reported honestly: the `cbor.deserialise` controls
are cheaper (0.18M / 1.07M) with no crossover at width, since deserialise is
a builtin and the acceptor is interpreted. Case B is a capability case, not a
cost case, and §11.4 says so — an earlier "materialisation is priced by the
whole item" claim was removed because the measurement refutes it for datums.

The capability is real, and it closes #567's residual. #567 screened
top-level bignum-headed datums with a head-byte check and documented that
nested bignums — canonical at any depth — still aborted the script, deferring
the fix here. Under PV11 `ConstrData` takes a Word64, and Aiken stdlib's
`cbor.deserialise` computes `ix = tag - 121` with no range guard, so any CBOR
tag below 121 aborts. The recursive acceptor now declines instead, verified
for a bignum as a map key, first-in-list, mid-list, at depth 5, and inside
tag-102. `is_canonical_plutus_data_v1`'s verdict is provably unchanged, so
L1 parity and #567's AC4 hold: canonical and materialisable stay separate
questions.

Case C — native-script checkpointable pushdown. Traversal 1.42M, checkpoint
and resume 1.79M, recursive-checker control 1.26M. The cursor is 87 bytes,
constant across scripts, `pub opaque` with a private decoder and only the
commitment-taking resume exported — #570's §10.6 shape preserved.

Two consensus divergences from the definitional checker, both caught by
review and both fixed
- The depth bound counted frames where `native_script_v1` counts nodes with a
  leaf at depth 1, so the pushdown admitted depth 17 while the checker refused
  it. On 16 nested `all` around one signature the checker returned None and
  the pushdown returned Some(True). Fixed with an explicit
  `max_native_script_frames = max_native_script_depth - 1`, and the agreement
  test now spans depths 1, 2, 15 and 16 rather than stopping at 3, with the
  other side pinned so the fix cannot over-refuse.
- `required` carried an upper bound the definition does not have, so
  `at_least(33, [signature])` — which the checker evaluates to Some(False) —
  aborted instead. A script the definition calls invalid could not be
  adjudicated at all. `required` is now capped rather than bounded: anything
  above the node count maps onto `unsatisfiable_required`, which preserves the
  verdict because `satisfied` can never reach it, while keeping the frame's
  wire scalar three bytes wide.

Guard coverage follows §9.5's discipline. §11.5 enumerates 36 refusals — 29
isolated, 7 backstops — reconciled against the 71 `expect` sites in the new
modules, with every backstop proven by neutralisation rather than argued. The
first recount said 15; auditing found 21 more, including one whose stated
"checked one step earlier" rebuttal was simply false.

Also fixed in review: the cursor's array header spelled `88` over seven
elements, so the wire form was not decodable CBOR — now `87`, with a test
that decodes it; the resume test could not detect a restart-from-zero, now
budgeted at exactly the remaining work and pinned both ways;
`datum_alternative_at_v1` aborted where §11 promises None, now guarded like
its two siblings; and the §5.6 citations for an output-value name cap were
re-pointed to §5.5, which now states the basis it was missing.

Note for future neutralisation work: deleting a guard whose constrained value
has no other consumer makes Aiken erase the whole computation, which reddens
many tests for the wrong reason. Weaken the predicate instead.

Verification: fork suite 2112 checks / 47 errors from a 2028/47 baseline
established by a detached worktree at 92fcffda, with the failing-NAME set
byte-identical — none of the 47 cleared, none added. Stock aiken check
--skip-tests: 0 errors. All seven touched .ak files are aiken fmt clean;
#570's modules were not touched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): machine walk core — authenticate-once, walk-derived item access, resumable checkpoints (#570)

The Phase-3a machine walk. Lazy per-field authenticate-once against the flat
hash, then three-tier offset-and-slice item access with no offset table: every
read is walk-derived from the authenticated bytes themselves, so there is no
second data structure to trust or dispute. Resumable checkpoints carry
positions, never bytes.

New lib/midgard/native-tx-machine-walk-v1.ak, plus §10 written into
docs/spec/midgard-tx.md (§10.1–§10.8), which #566 reserved for this ticket.

Measured, not asserted
- Authenticate-once (AC1): one open serving 64 reads costs 8,782,831 mem;
  re-opening the door per item costs 13,275,371 — over the 13,200,000-mem
  GOAL_SPEC §3.3 basis. Authenticate-once is what puts a 64-item field walk
  inside a transaction, with 33% headroom. Holding relocation constant and
  varying only door-opens gives 9,790,000 vs 13,275,371, so the verdict is not
  a fixture artifact; the 4.49M gap decomposes as ~3.48M door-opens plus
  ~1.01M access pattern, and all four rows now ship as tests so §10.7's
  re-take is reproducible from the suite.
- Arithmetic slice (AC3): spend_input_at at index 0 costs 7,827,953 mem and at
  index 295 costs 7,828,553 — 600 units across 295 positions, assertion
  residue. The variable-width control costs 59,704 mem per index step, about
  29,400x.

Resume carries positions only (AC2). A walk pauses at item 7 of 20 and resumes
in a follow-on transaction under a different carriage tier with a budget of
exactly the 13 remaining items, so a walk that restarted at zero would run
short; the both-ways pin confirms one fewer fails. Two preimages with the same
widths and disjoint content walked to the same position produce byte-identical
53-byte checkpoints.

A redeemer-controlled position hole, closed structurally
- resume_field_walk originally took a plain checkpoint argument, letting a
  caller supply a prover-chosen position — and a variable-width position is
  not recomputable, so nothing downstream could catch it. Making that function
  private was not enough: FieldWalkCheckpointV1 was a plain pub type, so its
  constructor was exported and walk_next/walk_skip/walk_fold accepted any
  checkpoint. A probe using only the public API built a literal checkpoint at
  offset 5 and read bytes from inside an item's payload with no commitment
  check at all.
- The type is now pub opaque and the decoder is private, so a position can only
  be derived, advanced, or returned by the commitment-checked resume. The probe
  no longer compiles. §10.6 and the module header now state exactly what the
  type system enforces, and separately what a library cannot enforce — where
  the caller's committed digest comes from, which stays normative on dispute
  entry points.

Guard coverage is now a property, not a claim
- Six guards documented in §10 had zero coverage: their negative vectors were
  tripping a deeper guard first, so the named guard could have been deleted
  with CI still green. Every refusal was audited by neutralising it one at a
  time and requiring exactly one test to go red.
- §10.8 enumerates all 23 refusals: 16 with isolating vectors, 7 as backstops
  that are unreachable-as-refusers, each naming the earlier check that makes it
  so. §9.5 admits exactly those two categories — uncovered is not one.
- Related: seven fail vectors were first written as `let _x = guard(...)`,
  which Aiken erases entirely, so none of them ran. Every negative now consumes
  its guard's result.
- v1_c20_script_item_does_not_open_as_field_7 was green for the wrong reason —
  a 34-byte item can never satisfy field 7's stride, so it was refused by the
  wrapper check rather than by the field hash. Rebuilt from a structurally
  valid 101-byte item so only the hash comparison can refuse it; neutralising
  that comparison now turns both directions red.

Scope
- 34 of the 37 counted-opening reds are deferred with cause: the 27
  validation-machine failures are control-type redesigns across 15 verify_item
  and 20 verify_chunk sites whose datums thread item_count/item_index/
  chunk_index/frontier into successor encodings (the machine lane, #572 AC4),
  and the 7 input-no-idx failures are Q13 (#575 AC1). Neither is a call-site
  swap. The 3 user_events/tx_order_v1 reds are owned by no ticket and are
  raised separately rather than deferred again.

Verification: fork suite 2028 checks / 47 errors from a 1983/48 baseline. The
failing-NAME set was diffed against a rebuilt HEAD state, not just counted:
exactly one cleared (the intended C20 rebind) and zero added. Stock aiken check
--skip-tests: 0 errors. §11 correctly absent — it is #571's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(core,onchain): per-field cross-language golden vectors for all nine fields (#569)

The Phase-2 tail: per-field golden-vector suites over the sum-type twins,
extending #568's channel rather than reinventing it.

New surface
- demo/midgard-core/src/codec/native-tx-field-items-v1.ts — the nine per-field
  §5.3 item encoders and §5.1 per-field preimage producers, TS twins of
  preimages.ak / components.ak. Fields 2 and 6 reuse the existing canonical
  encoders rather than re-spelling them.
- A second generated channel (generator + vector definitions + JSON fixture +
  a 62-test Aiken module), wired to package scripts and the CI gate exactly as
  #568's is, with the shared tail factored into scripts/golden-channel.mjs.

Coverage: each field gets envelope, §4 commitment, header, extents and reads,
plus a producer round-trip — the only cross-language proof available for
fields 2 and 5, whose items are whole records. Boundaries: fixed indices
0/23/24/255/256/65535, the two-byte header at 24 items, the MidgardV1 tag
18 80, all seven purpose tags, mint ordering including burns, and §6.2
bignum/constr-128 datums pinned as bytes — never deserialised, since under
PV11 they are canonical but not materialisable.

The straddle vector was pinning an unreachable configuration
- It used 400 field-0 items, but §5.4 caps field 0 at 296 spend inputs, so its
  largest admissible preimage is 11,843 bytes — under the 14,336 tier-1 bound.
  Field 0 can never reach tier 3, so the headline straddle proved nothing.
- Moved to field 1 (same stride-40 encoder, byte-derived bound 819). At 400
  items the preimage is 16,003 bytes, and item 397 spans [15,885, 15,923)
  across K = 15,900 while neighbours 396 and 398 sit wholly inside one chunk.
- Reachability is now asserted by the generator rather than left to prose:
  three guards refuse an unreachable field, a non-straddling item index, and a
  repeat count that drops the preimage under K. All three were proven to bite.

§5.6 ordering was enforced on one twin only
- preimages.ak now enforces asset-name and policy-id ordering on the producer
  side, carrying previous_* through the walk as the decoders already do. Four
  generated Aiken fail negatives twin the TS ones — both levels, both modes.

Scope
- Two goldens cleared: golden_midgard_core_native_preimage_cbor_decoders and
  canonical_redeemer_bridge_golden_vector_is_stable, both hand-written grammar
  vectors recomputed from the new producers rather than hand-edited.
- The remaining cross-language reds are NOT vector regeneration. They are red
  because the TS production path still emits minimal output indices and
  counted commitments; swapping deriveMidgardNativeFieldCollectionV1 /
  deriveNativeTxBodyCompact changes preimage bytes, field hashes and tx-ids
  across ~20 consumer files. That is the Phase-5 family rebind (#575–#578),
  and a scope note naming the TS entry points now sits on those tickets so the
  work is not orphaned. The v1_c20_6/7 pair additionally needs re-derived
  measured Cardano boundaries — a measurement, not a vector.
- EMPTY_SPEND_INPUTS_HASH stays counted. It is derived, not literal, so it
  flips when the consumer path swaps; and the gitignored plutus.json the
  fault-proof emulator executes cannot be settled without the blueprint
  regeneration fenced to #579. The tripwire test still bites at the swap.

Verification
- Fork suite 1983 checks / 48 errors, against a re-established 1921/50
  baseline at 129a95c2. Failing-name diff: exactly two removals, zero
  additions — #570's 37 machine-lane failures fully intact.
- Stock aiken check --skip-tests: 0 errors. midgard-core 441, midgard-sdk 185;
  typecheck and eslint --max-warnings=0 clean on both.
- The channel is closed on both sides: regenerating from a deliberately
  drifted producer makes --check pass but turns Aiken red, so the Aiken suite
  is an independent check rather than a mirror. #568's channel was re-verified
  to still pass and still bite after the shared-tail extraction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(onchain): enforce the pexcludes non-membership proof

`validators/pexcludes.ak` bound `mpf.insert` with `let _excluded`. Aiken fully
ignores unused let-bindings, so the call -- and the `expect excluding(key,
proof) == self.root` inside it, which IS the non-membership proof -- was
compiled away. The `exclusion` validator fell through to `True` for any
`[root, key, proof]` redeemer of the right shape, so a prover could forge a
non-existent-input fraud proof against a valid block and slash an honest
operator.

Bind with `expect`, the form already used at
`lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/transition-trace/proof.ak:671`.

The compiled withdraw script goes from 374 to 2977 bytes: the proof walk
previously occupied zero bytes on chain. Measured against a pristine build of
the same commit with the same compiler, exactly five validators move --
`pexcludes.exclusion` plus the four steps that embed its hash constant
(`no_input/step_03`, `no_input/step_04`, `no_reference_input/step_03`,
`no_reference_input/step_04`).

  pexcludes.exclusion  5a06db38b22c52ca7d1789f16c1819da03b15171efe245ef18ad7af6
                    -> a9ec251d6476217b1abccd5f035dec1272a4b04f640f503fca9e734d

`plutarch_pexcludes*` locates the withdraw redeemer *by* that constant, so the
pin move is required for the fix to take effect. Both `env/default.ak` and
`env/testnet.ak` are updated and re-verified against real builds of each env.

Adds the first tests this validator has ever had: a bogus proof against an
unproven root must be rejected (this test fails on the unfixed validator), and
a genuine non-membership witness must still be accepted. The defect survived
because the delegating steps only field-match the redeemer -- all cryptography
lived here, and nothing exercised it.

Gates: full typecheck clean; dual-compiler blueprint agreement clean (393
validators byte-identical across stock v1.1.22 and fork v1.1.23); pexcludes and
both delegating families pass. The §4.4 journey regression has NOT been run.

Pre-existing defect from dbfa7426; unrelated to #567.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(core,sdk): TS carriage/view sum-type twins and the cross-language golden channel (#568)

The shared Phase-2 head: TS twins of the Phase-1 types so off-chain and
on-chain encodings cannot silently diverge.

New surface
- demo/midgard-core/src/codec/native-tx-field-access-v1.ts — the TS twin of
  native-tx-field-access-v1.ak: §5.1 envelope grammar (fail-closed both
  directions), §4 flat commitment, the §5.3 stride table, §5.4/§8.3 constants,
  the MidgardFieldCarriageV1 / MidgardFieldViewV1 unions, the off-chain door
  with straddle-aware lazy-verify accessors, §8.4 chunk split, and the §8.6
  certificate and asset-name derivation.
- demo/midgard-sdk/src/native-tx-field-access-v1.ts — the Plutus wire twins
  with frozen Constr-index pins.
- A generated golden channel (generator + JSON fixture + generated Aiken
  module) that #569's per-field fan-out extends rather than reinvents, wired
  to a package script and a CI gate.

Two defects caught before landing
- The tier-3 off-chain door authenticated nothing against the field
  commitment: a certificate over 600 forged items, handed the honest
  commitment of a different preimage, returned the forged bytes as
  authenticated. buildMidgardChunkedFieldViewV1 now takes a required
  expectedCommitment and hashes the concatenated chunks against it after the
  §8.4 structural checks. Both view constructors require it, so no
  unauthenticated path remains. Full authentication necessarily hashes every
  chunk — §4 commits the whole preimage under one flat hash with no Merkle
  structure to open a single chunk against — so the on-chain and off-chain
  acceptance sets are now identical, reached by different routes: on-chain the
  certificate token carries the mint policy's check, off-chain the door does
  it directly. Per-chunk lazy digest verification is unchanged.
- The first SDK draft used the house Data.Tuple spelling, which emits
  Constr 0 [Constr 0 [B]] — correct tag, undecodable by the Aiken door. A
  constructor-index check alone would have missed it, so both sides now assert
  exact hex.

The golden channel's tier-3 chunk digests were pinned as literals neither
language recomputed. The payload is now reproducible from a 256-byte seed
block (the filler has period 256, so 512 hex chars replace 16 KiB, with a
generator-side assertion that the compaction is lossless), and both sides
rebuild it and recompute blake2b_256 per chunk.

Also: the stale counted empty-field pin eb25ed4a… in zero-input/step-02
becomes the flat 45b0cfc2… (test line only, no ABI impact); core's domain
types take the Midgard prefix their file-siblings carry, so they no longer
collide with the SDK schema exports of the same name.

Scope
- Of the 14 stale cross-language goldens #567 left, exactly one is fixable
  from shared grammar (empty_spend_inputs_hash_matches_the_offchain_constant,
  since the empty preimage 80 is field-independent). The other 13 each fail on
  a per-field §5.3 item encoding and need the nine per-field producers — #569,
  except v1_c20_6_c20_7_field_directory_and_witness_tuple_are_exact, which
  fails on counted-opening machinery and is #570's.
- EMPTY_SPEND_INPUTS_HASH in the SDK stays counted deliberately: the gitignored
  plutus.json the emulator executes is still the pre-#567 blueprint, so
  re-pointing it before #569's producers and #579's blueprint regeneration
  would break the fault-proof emulator. A tripwire test goes red when #569
  lands.

Verification
- Aiken fork 1919 checks / 50 errors, from 1895/51 at HEAD. Failing-name diff
  against HEAD is exactly one removal and zero additions.
- Stock aiken check --skip-tests: 0 errors.
- midgard-core 43 files/381 tests, midgard-sdk 28/185, lucid-midgard 19/162,
  midgard-validation 46/239, midgard-fault-proofs 341/342 (the one red is
  pre-existing at HEAD, owned by #570). Both dists rebuild; typecheck and
  eslint --max-warnings=0 clean on both packages.
- The golden --check gate was proven to bite four ways: hand-edited Aiken
  golden, a perturbed JSON constant, a flipped hex nibble, and a perturbed
  chunk digest — the last of which the pre-fix assertion set passed blind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): flat field-hash core scheme swap — nine flat commitments, one field-access door, canonicity re-pin (#567)

All nine compact-tx per-field commitments become flat blake2b-256 over raw
canonical enveloped field-preimage bytes, per docs/spec/midgard-tx.md.

The one door
- New lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak exposes the single
  authenticated_field_view: slice-only, straddle-aware, serving all three
  carriage tiers over FieldCarriageV1 (Inline/RawUtxo/Certified) and
  FieldViewV1 (Whole/Chunked) with lazy chunk verify. Positional hash
  extraction is private, so no caller can supply a free-standing field hash.
- bounded_collection_v1.from_items and codec.encode_native_byte_list removed;
  87 call sites rebound. verify_spend_inputs_preimage and spend_input_cbor_at
  deleted. One surviving production free-standing-hash consumer,
  input-witness.verified_spend_inputs_at, is documented and owned by the
  #575-#578 family rebind.
- One strict §5.1 header reader (minimal width, 9a rejected) now serves all
  eight envelope sites including mint; codec's general-CBOR reader keeps only
  its non-§5.1 role.

Preimage grammar
- Fixed 3-byte 19 XXXX output index; every other spelling rejected, so spend
  inputs are 38-byte items at stride 40. Mint moves off the raw map to the
  enveloped policy-item list. Fields 3/4 assert 28 bytes.
- Fixed-stride accessors now decode each item's own wrapper header rather than
  deriving the extent arithmetically. Without this, 81 ‖ 00 00 ‖ <28B> and
  81 ‖ ff ff ‖ <38B> opened through the door at byte-identical cost to the
  canonical spelling — two admissible commitments for one logical content,
  against §6.1. Both counterexamples are now regression vectors.
- Tier 3 enforces the §8.4 boundary (preimage_len > K) instead of merely
  total_length > 0, and field_item_count aborts for a variable-width tier-3
  view rather than returning the header's unauthenticated number.

Canonicity re-pin
- New lib/midgard/canonical-plutus-data-v1.ak re-pins the predicate to
  serialiseData's image: bignum tags 2/3 and constr tag 102 are canonical,
  restoring L1 parity.
- The materialisation path screens bignum-headed datums so it declines rather
  than aborting. This is deliberately separate from the canonicity predicate:
  bignums are canonical, they just cannot be materialised through the stdlib
  decoder at protocol version 11, where ConstrData takes a Word64 and the
  decoder's ix = tag - 121 goes negative. Nested bignums remain canonical at
  any depth and still abort; the residual is documented, not papered over, and
  belongs to #571's Canonical-Data Acceptor.

No change to tx-id derivation or compact-tx shape. §10 and §11 not
implemented — deferred by design to #570 and #571.

Verification (fork runner, pty, brace selectors throughout)
- Full suite 1895 checks / 51 errors, from a 1774/0 baseline at ab97e571.
  All 51 are downstream by design and were adjudicated individually:
  validation_machine_v1 27, input_no_idx/step_02 7, native_tx_v1 6,
  native_tx 3, tx_order_v1 3, and five singletons — counted per-item Merkle
  openings owned by #570's machine lane, plus cross-language goldens that
  regenerate from the TS producer in #568/#569.
- Focused suites green: native_tx_field_access_v1 103/0,
  canonical_plutus_data_v1 10/0, script_context_v1 23/0,
  tx_field_receipt_v1 4/0.
- Stock aiken check --skip-tests: 0 errors.
- Every wrapper, boundary, and decline fix was demonstrated red before and
  green after.

Also: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md gains the §8.6 asset-name erratum pinning
blake2b_256(field_index ‖ tx_id), a §7.2 clarification that arithmetic
derivation locates an item but does not excuse reading its wrapper, and the
§8.4 boundary-is-enforced note. The aiken-contract-build skill records that
a bare -m module selector matches zero tests and exits 0 — a false green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(spec): Phase-0 review response — authority reconciliation, F05 acceptance re-scope, provenance corrections (#566)

Two review rounds against #566's six acceptance criteria, no blockers.

Authority layer
- docs/DOCUMENTATION_POLICY.md source hierarchy admits docs/spec/ as the
  implementation-normative layer over technical-spec/ on concrete detail;
  docs/spec/README.md restates the identical scope so the two documents
  express one rule.
- GOAL_SPEC §3.1(2) no longer claims midgard-tx.md defines the resumable
  walk, Value bookmark, or Canonical-Data Acceptor. midgard-tx.md §1
  reserves §10 (#570) and §11 (#571) as deferred-by-design instead, so the
  by-reference binding stays honest without pre-empting Phase 3.

F05 manifest (AC6 re-scope half)
- Q00, C21, W27 and the CG2 gate row carry the amended GOAL_SPEC acceptance
  wording, each retaining its counted-scheme acceptance verbatim as
  provenance per invariant 14. 186 rows, id sequence byte-identical to
  b6e600f6, zero removals.

Provenance and numeric corrections
- §8.3 K basis and tier-1 bound re-sourced: the original text attributed
  both to #556/#557 observations that do not exist. Restated against what
  #556 actually measures, with a mandatory Phase-4 cross-check on K.
- GOAL_SPEC §3.3 no longer claims no verdict flips under the 13.2M basis:
  Q10 at 40 inputs (11,312,784) and Q11 at 41 (11,465,641) do sit in the
  11.2M-13.2M band and flip. Mitigation stated — the headline Q1X-F6 result
  at the admissible 296-input shape does not move.
- Epoch provenance separated: the captured artifact is decision 0001's
  Conway epoch-645 snapshot; epoch 648 is #552/#563 corroboration, not a
  captured artifact.
- decisions/0004 module counts re-derived against the tree (46 Aiken, 30 TS
  — the drafted 15 was wrong) with reproducing commands cited.
- §5.3 enumerates language_tag and purpose_tag admissible values against
  both language twins; 496-vs-512 reserve arithmetic reworded; tier
  vocabulary conversion completed across GOAL_SPEC.

Verified green: manifest-quality (PASS 186/186, 0 defects), fault-proof
reconciliation (70 rows/49 open), status-role control (PASS), CG4 gate
(BLOCKED unchanged from baseline), prettier --check on all changed docs.
Scope fence honored: no plutus.json, catalogue/deployment registry,
ABI-freeze artifact, or blueprint regeneration — those are reserved for
#579.

feat(spec): flat field-hash reversion Phase 0 — docs/spec authority, GOAL_SPEC amendment, decisions/0004

Phase 0 of the compact-tx flat field-hash reversion (#566; spec #565;
decision trail: wayfinder map #552, twelve closed tickets).

New authority layer. docs/spec/README.md states the rule: a component

compliance landed with the floors at the datum-writing seam; blueprint

fix(node): scope DA governance floors to initialization, not config load

84bdbf2a enforced the Q63 governed floors inside `NodeConfig` loading.
That was the wrong seam. `DA_COMMITTEE_HEX`, `DA_OWNERS_HEX` and
`DA_THRESHOLD` are read by exactly one consumer — the bootstrap in
`deriveOperatorDaParams` — but `NodeConfig` is loaded by every subsystem,
so a stale deployment value failed config load for the whole process.

A checkout carrying the pre-Q63 `DA_THRESHOLD=1` in its `.env` therefore
could not load config at all, and the failure surfaced as an opaque
Effect ConfigError inside tests and subsystems that never touch DA:

  Invalid data at : "DA_THRESHOLD must be at least 2 to satisfy the
  governed threshold floor, received 1"

Config load now validates only what is malformed regardless of policy —
non-hex, ragged element widths, and out-of-order or duplicate entries in
a packed set, which the governor's `sorted_unique_*` walkers reject
outright. The governed floors stay fail-closed in `deriveOperatorDaParams`,
the one place a governor-invalid datum would actually be written, where
the real committee length is known even when it is derived from local
signers rather than configured — a case config load could never see.

No backdoor: a below-floor threshold, a one-member committee, and a lone
owner are all still refused, and are now pinned by an explicit regression
for the pre-Q63 `DA_THRESHOLD=1` shape. `tests/da-config-load.test.ts`
pins the other half — that those legacy values load without bricking
unrelated subsystems.

fix(da): adapt apply-flow consumers to the governed-params reference and close the Q63 gate

Q62's ApplyToStateQueue now carries da_params_ref_input_index and the
SDK apply builder requires the governed params; the node apply program,
the da-committee-node coordinator builder/submitter, and the watcher
indexer fixture adopt it in lockstep. The Q63 gate's three open-group
self-test fixtures re-point to strike their target group wherever it
lives (groups or openGroups) so none can no-op now that the rescue
groups closed; gate exits 0 with all nine groups measured (29 checks)
and the self-test still rejects every seed. Q62 manifest counts
restated against the published vocabulary; quality 186/186.
feat(da): non-retroactive committee rotation and partial-attestation rescue (Q62 + Q63c)

fix(node): require floor-compliant DA governance at bootstrap

Q63 (F04 §4) gave the DA params governor threshold floors —
`da_threshold >= max(2, ceil(2*committee_len/3))` and
`update_threshold >= max(2, ceil(2*owner_len/3))` — which make a 1-of-1
committee and a lone owner unrepresentable. The node's bootstrap still
built exactly that forbidden shape: a single-key committee, a single
owner, and both thresholds hardcoded to one.

Bootstrap now emits at least two committee members and two owners, with
both thresholds defaulted to the governed floor. All bound arithmetic is
delegated to the SDK twins (`governedThresholdFloor`,
`daParamsFloorViolations`) so it cannot drift from the validator, and
both sets are emitted sorted-unique to match the governor's
`sorted_unique_*` walkers.

The second key is explicit configuration, never invented:
`DA_COMMITTEE_HEX`/`DA_OWNERS_HEX` name a real committee and owner set in
a deployment, while `DA_COSIGNER_SEED_PHRASE` gives dev and emulator
bootstrap a locally held second key so one process can reach a genuine
2-of-2. With neither present, initialization fails closed rather than
falling back to the shape the governor rejects. The same floors are
enforced at config load so a bad value is reported where it can be read.

Attestation signing follows: the hardcoded single witness at index 0 is
replaced by one genuine Ed25519 signature per locally held key, with the
signer index looked up in the on-chain committee rather than assumed.

Fixtures pinning 1-of-1 are lifted to floor-compliant shapes, including
the Scalus suite that evaluates a real AddSignatures body through the
actual Plutus validator — now a true two-signature attestation.

The blueprint is deliberately not regenerated here; this lands green
against the old committed governor, which accepts >=2-of-N too.
